value.title: Seat identity provenance, phase 1: route inventory and capability bootstrap (PRD 003 req-10, F88)
value.summary: Every seat-authority route is listed and classified in a checked inventory, and a reviewed workshop chooses how each seat incarnation gets a private capability, so phase 2 can gate routes on it.

sections.name: summary
sections.value: req-10 is the root of every F88-class finding (C32). It's large: about 32 route pairs, several harnesses and clients, and a rollout. Phase 1 makes the target measurable (the inventory sensor) and decides the design (the workshop) before code. Phases 2 and later (bootstrap, then gating route classes, send-as first) are planned from the workshop.

sections.name: goals
value: Every seat-authority route is listed and classified in a checked inventory, and a reviewed workshop chooses how each seat incarnation gets a private capability, so phase 2 can gate routes on it.

sections.name: non_goals
value: Gating any route on the capability (phase 2 and later).

req-11 (who may designate the prime), a separate small plan.

value.claim: The F88 route inventory is a checked artifact, not a note. A machine-readable inventory (harness/scripts/route-inventory.json or similar) lists every daemon HTTP method and route pair at the shipping head, each classified as machine-public (by explicit policy, with the reason) or seat-authority, and for seat-authority routes: the route class (send-as, inbox claim, role and holder actions, outputs, activity, registration, controls, adoption), which identities it grants authority by (seat, parent, prime, holder, owner, recipient), and the guard it uses today (the F88 note's R, B, N, S, C or provenance exception). It starts from squirrel's F88 note (governance roles/security/outputs/2026-11/07-note-issue-f88.dd.json, 63 pairs at a0ec952) refreshed to current main, including routes added since (#149 requests close, #152 steering, #153 presence, #156 modal stalls).

A workshop decides the capability bootstrap, before any code. docs/plans/221-seat-provenance/workshops/001-capability-bootstrap.md compares at least these options and recommends one: (a) a per-incarnation secret minted by the daemon at spawn and delivered privately to that process only (an inherited fd, a 0600 file under the seat's private dir, or the spawn environment), stored only as a hash; (b) OS peer credentials on a Unix socket (pid and uid of the connecting process), checked against the registered incarnation; (c) both, peer credentials as bootstrap evidence and the secret as the control (req-10 says peer credentials are bootstrap evidence, not the whole control). For each it answers: how spawned, adopted, revived and hand-started seats get one; how the native Copilot extension, the OMP and Pi extensions, the shim (pij-cli) and the Claude, Codex and Copilot hooks present it; how it rotates on re-registration and dies with the incarnation; how a seat's subprocesses (bash tools) can or cannot use it; what an attacker holding the daemon key but not the capability can still do; the per-request cost; and the migration path (old clients during rollout). It never reissues a capability from identifiers a victim exposes in the roster.

Cost (AGENTS.md, resource cost is a correctness property). Phase 1 adds no daemon runtime cost: the inventory sensor runs per harness checks invocation (one route enumeration plus one JSON read), not per tick. The workshop must state the chosen design's per-request cost (for example one hash compare per seat-authority request) and any per-seat launch (none is acceptable per tick).

Docs and states. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md gains a short 'Seat authority' section pointing at the inventory; docs/difficulties.md records F88's status; the plan states phases 2 and later as follow-up waves to be planned from the workshop. docs/how/pij-rs-api.md documents new verbs and refusals; the skill's verb coverage tables carry them; `just ddocs-check` and `ddocs validate` on the project docs pass; the PR body has a `Delivers:` line.

sections.name: research_context
sections.value: F88 (security, pij-annual-squirrel, 07 Nov): a local caller holding the daemon key can present another seat's registered identifiers and get that seat's authority (32 caller-dependent and mixed route pairs; HIGH 9/10). Ruling C32 accepts F88-class residuals at registration strength until req-10 lands; #149, #152 and #153 each carry a Known limit naming req-10. #152 round 4 (kestrel) showed the concrete next residual: uncorrelated sends still accept an asserted session id. PRD 003 is still draft #112; req-10 is its must-have. The prime (08 Nov 04:45): start with the parts q-02 to q-04 don't touch, the per-incarnation capability bootstrap and the inventory of endpoints that check it.

value.risk: Two lanes edit the same CLI wiring or skill files.
value.mitigation: Rebase onto main before the PR; small diffs at the seam; pm-001 orders merges.

sections.name: execution_guardrails
value: Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon; never the live governance branch or the prod daemon.
Builds: your own target or `just shared-build`; CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0; -p scoping; stop under 25 GB free.
No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`; no node_modules, never symlinked (C25); TS proof is CI on the exact head.
Shared seams (crates/cli wiring, skills/pij): rebase onto main before the PR and keep edits minimal; don't fork the seam.
One push per review round; no pushes after the PR is out for verdicts unless a verdict asks.
